title: Why Routines Make Classroom Management Easier; Plus One Great Idea t-easier-plus-one-great-idea/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Comparing classroom procedures to a professional golfer's pre-shot routine, Linsin argues that well-established classroom routines free students from distraction and guesswork, letting them focus fully on learning while also reducing a teacher's daily workload. He explains that routines minimize wasted time, reduce minor frustrations and opportunities for misbehavior, and, once automated, allow the teacher to simply observe rather than constantly re-explain procedures. Borrowing an idea from colleague Rick Morris, he describes using music from old television theme songs to cue different classroom transitions, with the length of each song setting a fun, built-in time limit for students to complete the procedure. He notes this approach keeps routines from becoming joyless drudgery, turning them into engaging challenges that also build teamwork.
points: Well-taught classroom routines reduce distraction, guesswork, and opportunities for misbehavior throughout the day.
Automated routines lower a teacher's daily workload by eliminating the need to repeatedly give the same directions.
Using recognizable theme music to cue and time transitions turns routines into an engaging, self-limiting challenge for students.
Injecting levity into routines prevents them from becoming joyless drudgery while still maintaining high expectations.
quotes: Routines—also known as classroom procedures—rid students of distractions that waste time and interfere with learning. Guesswork is minimized.
Well-executed routines also save time and lessen a teacher’s workload.
For everything your students do in your classroom repetitively, there should be a routine.
Many years ago, Rick Morris shared with me the idea of using music from old television shows to initiate routines—with each piece of music prompting a different routine.
But what makes this idea really cool is that the length of each song is the amount of time students are given to complete the procedure.
Everyday routines are thus completed quickly and efficiently. Best of all, you don’t have to open your mouth. Just point your remote at a boom box and set the routine in motion.
